cards.title: Two CLI paths
items: API-backed commands call RunOperation synchronously; HTTP submissions create asynchronous jobs. Both acquire the operation scheduler.
Other CLI commands call domain packages directly. CLI mutation hooks provide their own Desktop checks, snapshots, and undo wrappers; they do not run as HTTP jobs.

cards.title: Collection safety
items: The API runtime classifies bound effects before execution. It serializes writes and excludes collection readers for collection or unresolved filesystem effects.
A fresh Desktop check precedes non-preview collection writes. Ordinary writes create a safety backup unless disabled, then record before/after history. Sync, creation, and undo own specialized paths.

cards.title: Persistence and tools
items: The library node groups Engine SQLite databases with operation-selected audio and artwork files. Database access uses a five-second busy timeout on each pooled connection.
Only affected files are preserved for undo. Failed acquisition workspaces remain retryable when they are the only changes.
godeps manages tool versions and optional installation. Fetch, tagging, and metadata suggestions invoke managed executables; this diagram does not imply every operation invokes a tool.

cards.title: Overview scope
items: Components group cooperating packages rather than enumerate every Go package. Identity, sync baselines, fingerprints, and staging accompany their owning library operations.
Library preferences use a separate SQLite state store. HTTP job state and retained SSE events are bounded in-memory data, not a durable job queue.

cards.title: Saved markers — working-tree addition
items: GET /v1/tracks/{id}/performance also resolves within opened-library routes. requestTrack validates identity, and collectionRead shares the collection barrier.
The handler opens m.db read-only and reads PerformanceData beatData, quickCues, and loops. djtools v0.1.1 decodes slots, names, colors, and positions in seconds without database access of its own.
Absent markers return empty arrays. Invalid data returns invalid_saved_performance; failed reads return saved_performance_unavailable. This endpoint performs no mutation, snapshot, or undo write.
These additions are outside the pinned committed source evidence. Their implementation is internal/api/performance.go and its behavioral test.

cards.title: Analysis and beat grids — after the pinned revision
items: internal/analysis decodes audio once through FFmpeg and combines windowed tactus tempo and mixedkey key candidates with beat-phase, downbeat and tempo-change fitting. internal/beatgrid converts results into Engine anchors, computes reviewed edits, and stores grids through djtools v0.1.3's native beatData codec.

The HTTP API and CLI share track.analyze, track.grid.update and the read-only grid edit endpoint; commands are track analyze, track grid update and track add --analyze. Engine CLI remains the only component that opens Engine databases. Committed in 050ada5 and b333e89.

cards.title: Custom tags — committed addition: companion ownership
items: Engine CLI owns the separate library-local .engine-cli/tags.db companion: named categories and values use opaque UUIDs; assignments use native Engine origin UUID/track-ID pairs. Embedded-file track.tags operations remain a different domain. The browser accesses neither database directly.

Taxonomy and assignment reads never create storage or remove unavailable assignments. Taxonomy reports live-origin counts and unavailable origins, while its revision remains the stored taxonomy/assignment revision. Collection mutations use the existing scheduler, fresh Desktop guard, safety backup and history.

cards.title: Custom tags — committed addition: recovery and synchronization
items: The enrolled companion participates in native database snapshots, explicit backup presence, conflict-sensitive undo, and portable library recovery. A first-write undo can restore companion absence. This is CLI-owned library state, not UI preferences or embedded audio metadata.

Sync carries UUID-defined taxonomy and origin-based assignments. Destination-only definitions remain except under explicit whole-library/root mirroring. Playlist mirrors never delete unrelated destination taxonomy. Distinct-identity normalized-name collisions and retained references to removed definitions block application; a generic conflict winner does not repair these constraints.

Engine, companion and identity/sync JSON publications are separate commits. A later publication failure retains pending history and reports history_recovery_required; it does not claim all-or-nothing cross-database atomicity. Unresolved history blocks later collection writes until explicit recovery.

cards.title: Metadata find/replace — bounded exact review
items: track.batch.find-replace and track batch find-replace share collection-only transformations of eight text fields across 1–500 explicit selectors. Native Go regular expressions provide Unicode case folding and capture expansion; literal mode keeps replacement dollars literal. Audio files and embedded tags are unchanged.

A read-only review binds normalized options, canonical library root, library UUID, resolved track IDs, native origins and current metadata. Apply checks the captured token before Desktop checks, snapshots and history, then rechecks inside one metadata transaction. Empty titles block the whole batch; failed writes roll back. Results return affected IDs without rereading committed entities.

Before hydration, source values are limited to 1 MiB each and 16 MiB of review evidence. Output is separately bounded to 1 MiB per field and 16 MiB per batch; native match-index storage and capture expansion are bounded before allocation. Cancellation is checked around native matching and during assembly. Oversized work fails with metadata_transform_too_large before mutation artifacts.

cards.title: Metadata capitalization — Unicode recipes and exact review
items: track.batch.capitalize and track batch capitalize apply upper, lower or title casing to eight selected collection text fields. Existing golang.org/x/text cases and language APIs own Unicode and BCP 47 semantics; an empty language uses language.Und rather than the host locale. Audio and embedded tags remain unchanged.

Exact consent binds canonical library root, UUID, resolved identities, native origins, options and current metadata. Checked preflight runs before Desktop protection, snapshot and history; application rechecks the token inside one transaction and returns affected IDs after commit without rereading entities.

SQL byte-length checks precede hydration. Source evidence and outputs are bounded to 1 MiB per field and 16 MiB per batch. Whole-field casing supplies EOF for contextual word endings, resets before bounded expansion retries, and observes cancellation between attempts. Invalid recipes, languages, UTF-8 and empty resulting titles cannot authorize a write.

cards.title: Native saved hot cues — committed API ownership
items: track.cue.inspect is a library read; track.cue.set and track.cue.clear are checked collection writes. Cobra exposes the same slot A–H, revision, position/name/color contract with readable output. The UI never opens Engine databases.

Preparation validates target, slot, exact native revision and encodable values before Desktop protection, safety snapshot and history. The protected transaction rechecks native interpretation and media identity, then changes only the target cue bytes and any initially absent unset beat header required for interpretation.

Native codec edits preserve unrelated cue slots, loops, opaque bytes and trailer fields. A successful write returns the exact track/slot/revision result constructed from the committed plan, without a fallible post-commit entity read.

cards.title: Rekordbox XML import — immutable review and native preparation
items: migrate.import and migrate import read server-local Rekordbox XML into a reviewed new root hierarchy. Preview is a collection read and does not enroll source storage. Explicit missing-media, native-conflict and unsupported-field policies determine each source disposition; complete extant imports refuse duplicate hierarchy creation, while partial imports disclose retained mappings, omissions and the new root.

One job owns immutable XML bytes, destination observations, native origins, media observations and decoded first-audio sample extents. Checked preparation binds exact consent before Desktop protection, snapshot and history. Expensive decoding stays outside the write transaction; native file identity, size/time and exact XML content are rechecked before application and again after acquiring its transaction.

Maintained djtools codecs encode supported native grids, fractional saved positions and explicit cue/loop slots. Unsupported meters do not become invented 4/4 grids; memory/load marks do not invent a main cue. Unsupported source fields remain in exact XML and require explicit review. Saved markers receive the disclosed neutral-white color, rather than an unverified imported RGB value.

cards.title: Preserved import evidence — separate publication and recovery
items: The native transaction creates metadata, performance data and ordered hierarchy together, with explicit reviewed reuse and skips. A success receipt projects the committed root/document IDs and actual counts only after native commit and source-archive publication both succeed; it does not perform a fallible post-commit entity reread.

CLI-owned .engine-cli/imports.db stores exact source XML and document-local selector to native-origin mappings. Named companion enrollment keeps imports independent of custom tags. Snapshots and presence-aware restore/Undo preserve or remove each companion independently; damaged or unreadable evidence fails closed.

Engine and archive publication are separate commits. A publication failure after the Engine commit retains pending recovery history and returns failure, rather than claiming atomic cross-database rollback. Library sync transfers exact documents and selected extant mappings, preserves historical destination evidence during mirror, and refuses conflicting immutable document or mapping identities.

cards.title: Playlist track ordering — exact native membership review
items: playlist.reorder and playlist reorder share native membership ordering. Preview resolves local tracks through the originTrackId/originDatabaseUuid pair and validates the full PlaylistEntity chain. Ambiguous origins, cycles, missing links and multiple heads fail closed; unresolved native memberships remain preserved in the chain.

The supplied view must follow native ascending or descending membership order. Selected displayed runs retain their internal order and hidden memberships between their endpoints; the planner translates the displayed drop gap into native links without assigning local track IDs as membership identities.

Read-only preview binds the canonical library root, library UUID, target identity/title/parent/edit timestamp, complete membership observations and exact move options to a plan token. Checked apply rejects stale or ineffective consent before safety artifacts and rebuilds the same plan within its write transaction.

Application changes only affected nextEntityId links and the target playlist timestamp, checks each affected row and commits once. Failed writes roll back. The result is constructed from the committed plan without a fallible post-commit entity read. cards.title: Custom track colors — recovery and synchronization
items: Shared native database snapshots preserve independent companion enrollment. Backup presence version 3 records colors separately from tags and imports. Older backup presence versions imply color absence; restoration validates required databases before publication. Existing history and Undo preserve before-images, including first-enrollment absence.

Collection removal prunes only origins actually removed within that history boundary, retaining earlier unavailable assignments. Duplicate merge keeps an assigned survivor color, otherwise inherits one unambiguous removed color; conflicting removed colors are refused before safety enrollment.

cards.title: Retained-file PCM — direct HTTP and process ownership
items: The root HTTP server owns one in-memory PCM Store shared by its library servers. Track and staging creation resolve a regular source file under the collection read barrier, then release that barrier before decoding. Generations bind the captured library owner and retained descriptor; they are not asynchronous jobs, persistent companion state or Engine writes.

The Store limits generations, concurrent workers and its decoded-page cache. One active worker owns each retained file offset. FFmpeg receives the retained file on stdin with fixed first-audio decoding arguments; bounded stdout reads, cancellation and child Wait remain owned by the decoding call. Native descriptor and pathname identity, size and modification-time checks reject changed sources.

cards.title: PCM windows — observed extent and bounded teardown
items: Creation selects 44100 or 48000 Hz stereo interleaved float32 little-endian output. Metadata exposes an opaque generation ID and nullable frame length; window reads are bounded to 96000 frames. Decoded first-audio EOF establishes the authoritative end. An empty far seek does not prove EOF, and contradictory observations invalidate the generation.

Library-scoped metadata, window and release requests use the captured generation owner. Release and server shutdown cancel active work, join owned workers and close retained descriptors; idle generations expire. Cancellation closes the stdout pipe before killing and waiting for the direct child. WaitDelay bounds inherited stderr drain; this does not claim descendant process-tree termination.

Reviewed committed evidence 067f3b9fb30f3c2f45e0e4bc32bd8fb9b00fbbd0: internal/api/pcm.go:96-164; internal/pcm/decode.go:80-138; internal/pcm/window.go:9-107; internal/pcm/lifecycle.go:5-65. Native CI qualification is recorded separately; these cards describe committed implementation rather than asserting all-platform acceptance.

cards.title: Staging manifest publication — retained rooted handles
items: Staging writes preserve the current manifest through the existing history.Preserve call, then write, sync and close a unique temporary file under os.Root before publishing it. Unix retains rooted rename followed by directory synchronization; publication and close failures remain errors.

Windows retains the confined parent and opens the temporary source relative to its directory handle. It rejects source reparse points and replaces the manifest through a native relative-handle rename opened with WRITE_THROUGH. The documented rename-metadata durability guarantee is NTFS-specific; this does not promise identical physical durability across Windows filesystems.

Verification does not repair the collection or enroll snapshots and Undo; existing collection-read and job ownership remains unchanged.

cards.title: Intake ownership — committed service topology
items: The original overview was pinned to b85be4d87dc1045eca6133f6868e0b13f7bceb62. Its existing components have been traced again at 6f724a545fa0944deef7d8e260d0d403549d2d42; historical supplemental cards and their individual pins are preserved verbatim. Their statements about unchanged topology describe those historical additions, not the new intake actors shown here.

One API-owned registry is shared by opened-library servers. An enrolled library has a preparation service independent of individual HTTP requests. Opening does not enroll an absent queue. Initial receipt reconciliation precedes eligible FIFO preparation; a manually paused, restored or unresolved queue does not silently resume.

A native SQLite worker owner excludes competing preparation without holding the live queue write transaction across media work. Queue storage also holds a native observation lease. Replacement stops and joins the local worker before acquiring source/destination exclusion and collection/History ownership; exclusion is retained through publication or rollback and released before reopening.

cards.title: Intake persistence — independent publication evidence
items: The live intake journal records source identity/version, attempt, staging reservation, cancellation, durable import intent and exact returned Track ID. The retained staging manifest and copy are separate publications. Quiet time is only an observation heuristic; the retained regular source identity, size and mtime are checked around copying. Original source files remain untouched.

A reviewed intake import enters the ordinary collection-write Desktop, safety backup and History path. Durable intent precedes Engine writes; the exact Track receipt precedes History After capture. These are independent commits, not a distributed atomic transaction. Reconciliation never resubmits an import.

Ordinary collection History/Undo excludes the live intake journal so receipts survive Undo. Explicit backup includes intake presence and data; replacing that data marks it restored/paused. Explicit Resume first reconciles retained import evidence. Operational worker ownership is never snapshotted.

cards.title: Smartlist coherence
items: ReadSmartlistSafe owns a library-local observation lease. Existing history storage shares one SQLite owner across overlapping in-process readers; cross-process publication remains excluded until the last lease closes. Cancelling the first reader does not release another reader's lease.

An unenrolled library is read optimistically without creating history storage. If enrollment appears during the read, the result is discarded and the side-effect-free callback is repeated under the owner. A durable pending repair refuses observation; reads never recover it implicitly.

API collection-read metadata and native preparation lookups use this owner. Audio and PCM preparation retain their opened regular file across lookup, close discarded retry handles, and release observation before streaming or decoding. The API's collection scheduler remains a separate owner.

cards.title: Smartlist repair ownership
items: Engine CLI owns native Smartlist detection, temporally proven linkage, historical deletion attribution, staged images, exact plan tokens, publication and recovery. HTTP clients submit catalog operations; Engine database access remains CLI-owned.

library.smartlist-repair.preview is a coherent read. apply requires the reviewed plan_token and fresh Desktop protection; recover also requires fresh Desktop protection. Both use the repair publisher's exclusive history owner and immutable originals rather than generic AutoBackup or history.Run.

Reconnection gets a selective repair Undo entry. Proven deletion damage amends that original deletion's Before/After evidence so its existing one-step Undo remains the owner. An unattributed damaged component is removed without fabricated Undo; unrelated native rows and existing unrelated historical damage remain preserved.

cards.title: Coherent intake observation
items: Existing retained import receipts are observed while holding the native History owner before the intake worker owner, matching import lock order. A live History publisher is waited for cancellably rather than reported as a recovery failure.

The observer rereads the current ImportIntent tuple (item_id, history_id and persisted track_id receipt) and conditionally updates matching Item state after both owners are held. Resume retains this coherent observation boundary until reconciliation succeeds and suspension is cleared. Engine publication, queue receipts and History completion remain independent commits.

A queue without retained import intents does not enroll or wait on History merely to prepare sources. Missing History is identified before observation and checked again under the worker owner; unresolved missing or incomplete evidence still requires recovery.
Service shutdown cancels an initial History wait and joins the worker without publishing successful initial readiness or recording cancellation as a worker failure.

Import review opens its intake service before entering the shared Smartlist-safe read boundary. Only its database review callback, inside Service.Use, takes that read lease. At the original 6c8135c evidence revision, a live publisher or pending repair refused review; current reader ownership is described in the Cancellable collection reads supplement below; explicit import remains in the existing Desktop-protected History publication path.

cards.title: Cancellable collection reads
items: Public Smartlist-safe collection reads, including intake import review, wait cancellably for an existing History publisher. Completed import receipt reconciliation therefore does not make an immediate collection refresh fail merely because it briefly retains History.

A pending per-library read owner is published before native acquisition. The process-global readers mutex is released during the native wait, so unrelated libraries and existing readers can make progress. Overlapping readers share one retained native lease.

Each waiting reader can cancel independently. A cancelled first acquirer removes its pending owner and wakes surviving waiters to retry. Once acquired, the native lease is detached from that first reader context and remains until its last reader releases it.

Pending repair detected before acquisition refuses immediately; pending repair is checked again after acquisition before any observation. Reads do not recover or apply repair. Private History List and mutation acquisition retain fail-fast behavior; Desktop protection, snapshots and Undo publication remain unchanged.

cards.title: Watched discovery extends intake ownership
items: The existing intake Service retains one native discovery owner per library. fsnotify hints and periodic full reconciliation observe canonical roots pinned to native identity; descendant links and target-library operational storage are refused. Overlapping roots and hard links share a version and handoff.

Discovery deduplicates registrations by native directory identity. Changed coverage is installed and postvalidated on a successor backend before publication, followed by an immediate full scan. Unchanged verified coverage remains stable. Each backend owns a cancellable event drain that is joined on retirement.

A short native state owner spans pending intent, queue insertion or association, and final link. The original queue source tuple remains immutable. Crash recovery can retain unknown creator provenance; it does not invent exactly-once publication or retry terminal items.

Discovery and source-preserving preparation do not import. Explicit reviewed import still owns Desktop checks, safety backup and ordinary History; decoded-frame audio admission remains a separate collection gate.

Explicit replacement validates and preserves the portable watch/intake pair while the state owner is retained. Its native authority fence commits before the first live replacement. Ordinary collection Undo excludes both live journals; replacement Undo enrolls the paired images. Restored absence remains absent and still requires explicit watch activation.

Source evidence: 05102c1cc0c4b1db00826dc007753b544162e79b. Watch discovery lifecycle and ownership diagrams describe the additional owners; the historical intake cards retain their original revision scope.

cards.title: Offline Desktop fixture capture — shared CLI and HTTP primitive
items: library fixture capture accepts explicitly offline before/after handovers and a new private output directory. Retained native ancestor identities reject input/output containment before output creation, including case-insensitive aliases without conflating distinct native names. Retained read-only handles archive all observed files and database sidecars before SQLite opens working databases; complete path, native-identity, size, timestamp and content observations are checked before and after processing. Observed changes fail capture. This does not establish live-copy atomicity.

Distinct working copies recover copied rollback journals or WAL through SQLite, then the existing native SQLite backup primitive produces standalone snapshots. JSON exports retain SQL storage types, NULL and exact TEXT/BLOB bytes; unsupported filenames or schema metadata and ambiguous sidecar families fail closed. Native Smartlist, Playlist and PlaylistEntity comparisons retain complete rows and link changes. Failed outputs remain private evidence and cannot be reused.

The synchronous CLI command and library.fixture.capture HTTP job delegate to the same capture primitive. API capture retains a catalog read effect and shared collection-read token, while its output writes serialize through the existing write queue. Queued cancellation creates no output; later failures retain private incomplete evidence and stable typed causes. Neither entrypoint opens original databases through SQLite, selects a library, enrolls companions, or creates normal collection backups or Undo history. Raw evidence requires privacy review; captured rule bytes and screenshot memberships do not establish an evaluator.

cards.title: Native maintainer handoff — qualification and Desktop acceptance
items: Dispatch with full committed source and ancestor golden revisions. Native macOS arm64 and x64 jobs build a clean complete checkout, bind actual host/Go architecture, golden bytes and CLI/helper hashes, and refuse reused output namespaces. Source inventories must remain unchanged.

Observe all four baselines before the first repair in each independent seed: healthy, reconnect, unknown-removal and original-deletion. Apply reviewed tokens; verify complete native rows and exact History ownership; require zero-change preview/application without new Undo. Relocate with the old root absent and verify actual CLI track reads and scoped audio bytes against synthetic media.

Qualification exercises exact-ID reconnect repair Undo and original-deletion Undo with preview and History preservation. A separate delivery seed repeats the baseline barrier and repair checks and stays repaired. Archive only allowlisted synthetic libraries, executable CLI, instructions and delivery-specific Undo script; extract into a fresh namespace and reverify repaired rows and bundled CLI audio. Private full-row provenance remains outside the delivery archive.

Human Desktop evaluation records actual version/architecture, visible names, rules, memberships, sibling order and playback before Undo. Close Desktop before exact delivery-specific Undo, then reopen to record the two distinct restored states. Automated native qualification produces an acceptance candidate; desktop_accepted remains false until actual observations are reviewed.

cards.title: Shared dependency inspection and changes
items: tools.inspect reads each managed tool once and combines requirements with godeps version semantics. Each dependency has one highest minimum and observations for every requiring context, including Engine-managed tools. Missing, invalid or failed observations cannot establish readiness. Child processes receive their own managed dependency directory before the inherited PATH without mutating Engine's environment.

tools.dependencies.install and tools.dependencies.update each run as one serialized system operation across every known requiring context. Separately managed copies remain explicit internally. Existing native installers and verification retain ownership; the aggregate operation records successes and failures without adding a post-write inspection. The consumer requests a separate fresh tools.inspect read before reporting readiness.

cards.title: Native shared readers and exclusive publishers
items: ReadSmartlistSafe and ReadSmartlistProjection retain a native shared History lease for an enrolled library. Readers in separate processes can overlap; readers in one process share a reference-counted owner. The last reader releases that owner, independently of the first reader’s cancellation.

History publication takes an exclusive lease on the same empty lock database. The lock database must be an empty regular file using a rollback journal. Native acquisition remains cancellable where the caller requests waiting; mutating History operations keep their fail-fast policy.

ObserveEntries retains exclusive ownership while handing History entries to intake reconciliation. It is not the shared read lease. Intake preparation/import states and their recovery transitions do not change.

cards.title: Smartlist sync observes source, then owns destination
items: Sync captures the source native rows and projected Smartlist recovery evidence together, then releases source observation before inspecting or acquiring the destination. Preview computes the final destination graph without repairing either library.

Apply repeats the comparison under destination publication ownership before repair, backup or an ordinary History entry. Selected source rows, retained destination rows, conflict choices, mirror removals and native playlist identities determine one final graph. The final saved rows are also rehearsed against the destination’s declared Smartlist table constraints in isolated memory. Raw rule values and unchanged NULL cells are preserved.
The dedicated Library sync workflow describes this specialized path. It does not replace the ordinary collection-write safeguards.

cards.title: Read-only Smartlist membership
items: smartlist.tracks is a library-scoped collection read through the existing job and read barrier. Engine CLI validates native rules, compiles allowlisted columns/operators with bound values, then returns current matching tracks using the existing listing fields. It creates no PlaylistEntity rows, snapshot, Undo entry or persistent membership cache.

Saved Stems status observes regular files under the library Stems directory by origin identity. Desktop transient rendering queue state is outside this offline read. Captured metadata memberships are replayed; Stems tests explicitly reconstruct excluded file inputs. Unknown rules fail with smartlist_rules_unsupported instead of returning partial rows.

cards.title: Protected Smartlist removal
items: smartlist.rm owns one native transaction: park the target under its own UUID, relink its predecessor using unchanged nullable successor values, then delete only the saved definition. Native unique-link constraints stay enabled. Track, Playlist and PlaylistEntity rows are untouched; malformed or future rule bytes remain opaque.

The existing write job owns fresh Desktop protection, snapshot and History Undo. Exact Undo restores the removed definition and sibling links. The result returns the UUID and parent playlist ID without a post-commit read. No new scheduler, persistent store or actor is introduced.

cards.title: Reviewed Smartlist conversion
items: smartlist.convert.preview reads a coherent plan: source UUID, collision-free ordinary title, same parent and current matching count. Empty plans cannot apply; unsupported rules refuse. The plan token binds rule bytes, parent, name and ascending local track IDs.

smartlist.convert recomputes the plan inside one native transaction, appends the ordinary playlist after all mixed siblings and materializes native origin-key memberships. Names avoid semicolon path aliases across the entire ordinary hierarchy. Final native links are validated before commit. Source Smartlist and rules survive, and later metadata changes do not alter the new playlist membership.

Existing collection scheduling, fresh Desktop protection, snapshots and History Undo remain authoritative. Undo restores exact rows and links. The returned destination is captured before commit without a post-commit read. No new persistent store or scheduler is introduced.

cards.title: Protected Smartlist moves and mixed reordering
items: smartlist.move validates the source UUID, ordinary destination and mixed sibling anchor before changing any row. One transaction parks the source, joins its old predecessor past it, inserts it before the destination sibling and publishes its new parent. Final native graph validation precedes commit.

Rules and edit time remain opaque and unchanged, including malformed and future rules. Ordinary playlists, memberships and tracks are untouched. Invalid destinations, anchors, unchanged positions and name collisions refuse without publishing; exact History Undo restores all original links.

The existing collection-write owner retains fresh Desktop protection, snapshot and Undo. The result returns held UUID and parent values without a post-commit read. No new store, scheduler or actor is introduced.

cards.title: Automatic tools and upstream release checks
items: tools.inspect accepts check_updates:true to read official upstream release versions without installing software. Shared dependency rows carry website, available_version and update_error_code; updates_checked records completion. Release lookup failures retain installed observations and dependency readiness. FFmpeg and FFprobe share one release lookup; system package versions may differ from upstream.

The UI always submits supported auto_install parameters, overriding old saved opt-outs. Forms and operation dialogs omit the checkbox and installation-only consent. Collection, staged-file and explicit tool-change confirmations retain their existing scopes. Staging retries can enable installation over saved acquisition requests; tag inspection and artwork embedding also support auto_install.

The tool-management page shows a flat list with website links and installed/available versions. Entry, Check for updates and post-change reads request release checks. Existing component/session and CLI operation owners remain responsible; no database owner, machine or persistent store is added.
